summary: This Ramadan bonus episode (Ep 36) teaches two supplications of the Prophet ﷺ for anxiety and sorrow, two things tied to Amul Huzn, the Year of Sorrow. The first supplication (narrated by Ibn Mas'ud RA, Ahmad, sahih) is read and explained line by line: admitting that we are servants, that our forelock is in Allah's hand, that His decree is carried out and just, asking by all the names of Allah, and then asking that the Quran be the spring of the heart, the light of the chest, and what removes grief and anxiety. The second, taught to Abu Umamah RA who was sad and in debt, seeks refuge from anxiety, sorrow, weakness, laziness, miserliness, cowardice, the weight of debt and the domination of men. The ustaz closes with Al-Baqarah 2:38 and Yunus 10:57: trials will certainly come, but Allah's guidance and healing are guaranteed for believers.
keyPoints: The Prophet ﷺ promised that whoever recites the supplication of Ibn Mas'ud with full reflection will have their sorrow removed and replaced with joy, and he told his community to learn it.

The supplication has an order: admit servanthood, hand control to Allah, acknowledge His decree is just, call on His names, and only then ask, and what is asked is the Quran as a healing for the heart.
Huzn is sorrow over what has already happened, while ham is anxiety about what is to come. The devil is most active in attacking at the moment of sorrow.

The second supplication teaches us to seek refuge from anxiety, sorrow, weakness, laziness, cowardice, miserliness, the weight of debt and the domination of men, and Abu Umamah RA came out of his sorrow and debt.
Supplication does not replace effort: the Prophet ﷺ questioned Abu Umamah RA for sitting in the mosque outside prayer time, and debt should be avoided unless pressed.
Trials will not stop until death, but Allah's guidance (2:38) and the Quran as healing and mercy for believers (10:57) make us able to get through them.

chapters.title: Opening clip
chapters.summary: The lecture opens with a clip on how hard it is to say 'You are just with me' when struck by a great calamity.

chapters.title: Introduction: Ramadan, Amul Huzn and two supplications
chapters.summary: A bonus episode in Ramadan, on two supplications left out of the episodes on Khadijah's RA death and the Ta'if tragedy.

chapters.title: The book Hisnul Muslim
chapters.summary: The ustaz introduces Hisnul Muslim (Fortress of the Muslim) and its commentary, books he bought in Madinah and Mecca, which contain both supplications.

chapters.title: The first supplication: the Prophet's ﷺ promise
chapters.summary: Hadith of Ibn Mas'ud RA: whoever recites this supplication, Allah removes his sorrow and replaces it with joy. The supplication is read in full.

chapters.title: Allahumma: complaining straight to Allah
chapters.summary: A direct call to Allah; one may share with friends, but the peak is to Allah. The story of Prophet Yaqub AS in Surah Yusuf.

chapters.title: I am Your servant, the son of Your servant
chapters.summary: Trials humble the heart and remind us we are servants. We are part of a chain of servants since Prophet Adam AS, not special people.

chapters.title: My forelock is in Your hand
chapters.summary: The meaning of nasiyah, and its link to the frontal cortex, which governs decisions, emotions and self-control.

chapters.title: Your decree is carried out and just
chapters.summary: Calamity hits its target, the devil is most active in sorrow, and how heavy it is to say 'You are just' in the deepest grief.

chapters.title: Asking by all the names of Allah
chapters.summary: The etiquette of supplication: humble yourself first. The names of Allah are Allah's right and must not be added to. The names known to other creatures and those kept in the unseen.

chapters.title: The Quran: the spring of the heart and the light of the chest
chapters.summary: This supplication leads to action: being with the Quran. Why 'spring', 'light' and 'expanding', and the link to marhaban and rest.

chapters.title: Removing huzn and ham
chapters.summary: Huzn is sorrow over what has happened, ham is anxiety about what is to come. The story of a hospital patient and examples of anxiety about the future.

chapters.title: The second supplication: the story of Abu Umamah RA
chapters.summary: The Prophet ﷺ saw Abu Umamah RA sitting in the mosque outside prayer time. He said he was bound by sorrow and debt, and was taught the supplication.

chapters.title: Weakness, laziness, miserliness, cowardice and debt
chapters.summary: An explanation of each request in the second supplication, including why weakness and laziness are born of excessive fear.

chapters.title: Being alert to the people around you
chapters.summary: The Prophet ﷺ noticed a Companion who seemed 'off'. We need to keep ties, be an ear and a shoulder, and be alert to those carrying burdens alone.

chapters.title: The weight of debt
chapters.summary: Avoid debt unless pressed, debt institutions as a last resort, the effect of debt on the family, and a supplication for sufficient halal provision.

chapters.title: Closing: guidance and healing from Allah
chapters.summary: Al-Baqarah 2:38 and Yunus 10:57. A heart that returns to and relies on Allah, and a supplication to be held firm on the declaration of tawhid when the soul is taken.

books.context: A collection of supplications and remembrances from the Quran and Sunnah. The ustaz bought it in Madinah and Mecca for 3 riyals, and once bought 100 copies to give away. Both supplications in this lecture are in it, at the 30th and 35th according to the ustaz.
books.note: Author not named in the lecture: Sa'id bin Ali bin Wahf Al-Qahtani.

books.context: A commentary explaining each supplication in terms of meaning and historical context. The ustaz shared commentary on these supplications while working at a bank in 2011 and 2012.
An earlier Ramadan series explaining more than 100 names of Allah SWT.
Source of the first supplication (hadith of Ibn Mas'ud), graded sahih.
Among the sources of the second supplication, narrated through many routes.
Discusses huzn (sorrow) and the stations of the heart on the journey to Allah.
A commentary on Sahih Bukhari on supplications, including seeking refuge from anxiety, sorrow, weakness, laziness and debt.

people.context: Her death was one of the causes of Amul Huzn. The ustaz says this supplication was forgotten in the episode on her death.
Came to clean the Prophet ﷺ after the camel entrails were placed on his head.

people.role: Companion, narrator of the first supplication
people.context: Narrator of the hadith of sorrow. The ustaz reminds us he is also the narrator of the story of the camel entrails placed on the Prophet's ﷺ head during prostration.
His story in the 12th surah was revealed during Amul Huzn to comfort the Prophet ﷺ.
Complained of his sorrow and grief only to Allah when his own sons did not understand.
The chain of 'son of Your male servant and female servant' reaches them. Allah sent them down with guidance (Al-Baqarah 2:38).
Among the stories of earlier prophets that show a chain of servants who went through hardship.
Narrated the first supplication (Ahmad) and the second (Bukhari, among others).
Sat in the mosque outside prayer time because he was bound by sorrow and debt, and was taught the second supplication by the Prophet ﷺ.

lessons.title: Learn and memorise this supplication, because the Prophet ﷺ told us to
lessons.body: The Companions asked whether they should learn it, and the Prophet ﷺ told whoever heard it to learn it. The ustaz invites us to recite it every morning and with Quran recitation.

lessons.title: Pour it out directly to Allah, and there is no harm in sharing with friends
lessons.body: Looking for a listener who can lend an ear and a shoulder is fine, but the peak of confiding is to Allah alone and directly, like Prophet Yaqub AS.

lessons.title: Trials humble the heart and remind us we are servants
lessons.body: When we feel powerful and deserving, then everything is taken away, we are reminded that we are only servants, part of a chain of servants since Adam and Hawwa. Nothing is special except the title of servant of Allah.

lessons.title: Calamity hits its target and fits our capacity
lessons.body: The word for calamity comes from the root for 'target': it does not mistake its person. It is sent precisely, measured to our ability to bear it.

lessons.title: Beware when sad: the devil is most active
lessons.body: The devil works overtime when calamity strikes, planting 'if only' and 'why me', and comparisons with others, to take away the sense that Allah is just.

lessons.title: Etiquette of supplication: humble yourself before asking
lessons.body: Asking arrogantly and then saying the Lord does not hear is not good manners. This supplication teaches us to humble ourselves and call on Allah's names before asking.

lessons.title: The names of Allah are Allah's right; don't add to them
lessons.body: We name Allah only with names Allah has named Himself, as we do not say 'the Great Engineer'. Scholars differ over whether something is a name or an attribute, but adding new words is not allowed.

lessons.title: The Quran is a healing, but it needs to be asked for
lessons.body: Reading and hearing the Quran without this supplication may not touch the heart. This supplication asks for the Quran to be the spring of the heart, the light of the chest and the remover of grief.

lessons.title: Distinguish huzn and ham
lessons.body: Huzn is sorrow over what has happened and cannot be changed, ham is anxiety about what is to come. We cannot live without any anxiety at all, but excessive anxiety should be asked to be removed.

lessons.title: Pray but also get up: don't sit in surrender without effort
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ asked why Abu Umamah was sitting in the mosque outside prayer time. Religion tells us to work and move, and supplication lifts the spirit, it does not replace effort.

lessons.title: Be alert to the people around you
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ noticed and asked when he saw a Companion 'off'. We need to keep ties so we know when something is wrong, be an ear and a shoulder, and not be obsessed with ourselves.

lessons.title: Look at those worse off in worldly matters
lessons.body: Social media makes gratitude hard because we constantly see people who have more. The Prophet ﷺ taught us to look up in religion and down in worldly things.

lessons.title: Avoid debt unless pressed, and debt institutions are a last resort
lessons.body: Debt tightens slowly until it threatens family and sanity. The ustaz warns about 'buy now pay later' and easily approved loans, and stresses self-control.

lessons.title: Trials do not stop, but guidance and healing are guaranteed
lessons.body: Humans were created to be tested. Allah did not send us down without guidance (2:38), and the Quran is a healing and mercy for believers (10:57).

lessons.title: A heart that returns to and relies on Allah
lessons.body: The greatest victory is to be held firm on the declaration of tawhid when the soul is taken. A true heart returns to Allah (inabah) and relies on Him completely (tawakkul).

glossary.meaning: The Year of Sorrow, the year the Prophet ﷺ lost Khadijah RA and Abu Talib and went through the Ta'if incident.
The most beautiful names of Allah. They are Allah's right, not something humans may add to.
The forelock, meaning the whole front part of the head. To hold the nasiyah means to have complete control.
The spring of the heart: an image of a dry heart becoming fertile and blooming again with the Quran.
Sorrow over what has already happened and can no longer be changed (grief).
Anxiety and worry about what is to come (anxiety).
Weakness, being unable, and laziness. The ustaz links it to excessive fear and loss of motivation.
Cowardice and miserliness, two traits that block productivity. To move forward we need to be generous with time and energy.
The pressure and coercion of others, especially when unable to pay a debt.
Returning to Allah with repentance, together with tawakkul, meaning complete reliance on Him.

dalil.context: The verse in which Allah specifically says He is near and answers supplication. The ustaz links it to Ramadan as the month of supplication. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: [Prophet], if My servants ask you about Me, I am near. I respond to those who call Me, so let them respond to Me, and believe in Me, so that they may be guided.

dalil.context: The Prophet ﷺ promised that whoever recites this supplication, Allah removes his sorrow and replaces it with joy. The Companions asked whether they should learn it, and the Prophet ﷺ told whoever heard it to learn it. The ustaz says this supplication is in Hisnul Muslim, and he himself has experienced the effect of reciting it with the Quran.
dalil.translation: O Allah, I am Your servant, the son of Your male servant, the son of Your female servant. My forelock is in Your hand. Your judgement concerning me is carried out and Your decree concerning me is just. I ask You by every name that is Yours, by which You have named Yourself, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen: make the Quran the spring of my heart, the light of my chest, the remover of my sorrow and the departure of my anxiety.

dalil.context: Prophet Yaqub AS complained of his sorrow only to Allah when his own sons did not understand. The ustaz mentions verse 86 with some doubt.
dalil.translation: He said, ‘I plead my grief and sorrow before God. I have knowledge from God that you do not have.

dalil.context: The ustaz stresses that Allah's names are not limited to 99, and that we name Allah only with the names Allah Himself mentioned, without adding new ones like 'the Great Engineer'.
dalil.translation: Whoever preserves the 99 names of Allah will enter Paradise.

dalil.context: The Prophet ﷺ taught it to Abu Umamah RA, who was sad and in debt, to be recited morning and evening. Abu Umamah RA did so, and Allah removed his sorrow and settled his debt.
dalil.translation: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from anxiety and sorrow, from weakness and laziness, from cowardice and miserliness, from the weight of debt and the domination of men.

dalil.context: Working to support one's family is one of the greatest forms of generosity.
dalil.translation: The most weighty spending in Allah's sight is what is spent on one's family.

dalil.context: The ustaz relates it to social media, which makes gratitude hard.
dalil.translation: In religion look at those above you, in worldly matters look at those below you.

dalil.context: Used to invite us to be more alert to the less fortunate.
dalil.translation: Seek me among the weak ones in your community.

dalil.context: The ustaz also mentions that a person who dies in debt, even a martyr, has his soul held back.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ once declined to lead the funeral prayer for a Companion because a few dinars of his debt had not been settled.

dalil.context: According to the ustaz, the Prophet ﷺ said this supplication gives the strength to settle a debt even as large as a mountain.
dalil.translation: O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have forbidden, and enrich me by Your bounty so that I need no one but You.

dalil.context: The ustaz says Allah tests with hunger, fear and loss of life. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: We shall certainly test you with fear and hunger, and loss of property, lives, and crops. But [Prophet], give good news to those who are steadfast,

dalil.context: Humans were created to go through hardship upon hardship. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: that We have created man for toil and trial.

dalil.context: Allah sent Adam and Hawwa down with guidance. Whoever follows it need not fear excessively for the future and will not grieve.
dalil.translation: We said, ‘Get out, all of you! But when guidance comes from Me, as it certainly will, there will be no fear for those who follow My guidance nor will they grieve-

dalil.context: The story in Surah Al-Kahf: a boy who would become a disbeliever and wrongdoer, whom Allah took in childhood. It shows a little of the veil of destiny. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: The young boy had parents who were people of faith, and so, fearing he would trouble them through wickedness and disbelief,

dalil.context: Allah replaced that child with a better one. Parents do not know the wisdom when they grieve. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: we wished that their Lord should give them another child- purer and more compassionate- in his place.

dalil.context: The Quran is advice from the Lord, a healing for what is in the chests, guidance and mercy for the believers.
dalil.translation: People, a teaching from your Lord has come to you, a healing for what is in [your] hearts, and guidance and mercy for the believers.

dalil.context: Whoever believes in Allah, Allah guides his heart. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Misfortunes can only happen with God’s permission––He will guide the heart of anyone who believes in Him: God knows all things––

sirah.era: Amul Huzn: the Year of Sorrow, late Meccan phase
sirah.summary: This Ramadan bonus episode returns to Amul Huzn, the Prophet's ﷺ Year of Sorrow after the deaths of Khadijah RA and Abu Talib and the Ta'if incident, to draw out two supplications that can be a shield for the heart.

events.label: Background
events.title: Amul Huzn: the Year of Sorrow
events.desc: The ustaz wants to complete the supplications left out of the episodes on Khadijah's RA death and the Ta'if tragedy.

events.label: Prostration
events.title: Camel entrails placed on the Prophet's ﷺ head
events.desc: One of the saddest moments of his life, narrated by Abdullah ibn Mas'ud RA. Fatimah RA came to clean it off.

events.label: Revelation
events.title: Surah Yusuf revealed during Amul Huzn
events.desc: The story of Prophet Yaqub AS, who grieved until he lost his sight, comforted the Prophet ﷺ.

events.label: In the mosque
events.title: The Prophet ﷺ meets Abu Umamah RA
events.desc: The Prophet ﷺ noticed a Companion who did not look as usual and asked, then taught him the supplication.

events.label: Ta'if
events.title: The Prophet's ﷺ supplication at Ta'if
events.desc: The ustaz compares the supplication at Ta'if ('if You are not angry with me, I do not care') with the supplications in this lecture: full devotion and good thoughts of Allah.
